summary: The root كثر (kthr) signifies abundance, whether in quantity, number, or frequency. It describes something as much, many, numerous, or copious.
lane: كَثِيرٌ ذ (S, A, Msb, K) and (S, K) and and and and (K) Much; copious; abundant; many; numerous; multitudinous. (S, A, Msb, K.) You say خَيْرٌ كَثِيرٌ , and , Much, or abundant, good. (A.) And قَوْمٌ كَثِيرٌ A numerous party, or people: and هُمْ كَثِيرُونَ They are many. (S.) And رِجَالٌ كَثِيرٌ , and كَثِيرَةٌ , Many men: and نِسَآءٌ كَثِيرٌ , and كَثِيرَةٌ , Many women. (Yoo, ISh, Msb.) And عَدَدٌ , (S, Msb,) and, as some say, , (Msb,) and كَثِيرٌ , (K in art. بول , &c.) A large number. (S, Msb.) And غُبَارٌ Much dust: (S:) or much confused dust (K, TA) rising and diffusing itself: of the dial. of Hudheyl. (TA.) -b2- [ A large quantity, or number, مِنْ مَالٍ وَغَيْرِهِ of property, or cattle, &c. ] -b3- كَثِيرًا , as an adv., Much; often. (The lexicons passim.) -b4- رَجُلٌ كثيرٌ [in the TA كثر : probably the right reading is , q. v.:] A man whose ancestors are many, and whose high deeds are various. (L.) -b5- See also مُطَّرِدٌ .
